reason: Conversation 1 correctly identified the door interlock/latch system as the likely cause, gave sensible front-only checks (hooks, slots, button feel) with a proper high-voltage warning, incorporated the customer's door-sag observation, and escalated to a Bosch engineer without naming a part; its only flaw was the unsupported assumption that a 4-year-old unit is 'likely still under warranty'. Conversation 2 was safe but diagnostically poor: it pursued an overheat cut-out theory that doesn't fit the 'start indicator off, fan and light stop as if door opened' pattern, asked the customer to check vents he obviously couldn't see in a built-in housing, and then ignored his accurate door-switch reasoning with a repeated boilerplate reply that added nothing.
